claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

hospital_abroad.description: Whether the child is in hospital abroad.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions. Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children you're responsible for, and if so, how many children are you asking about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes! I'm asking about my son Alex. He's 8 years old and lives with me here at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you're asking about your son Alex, who is 8 years old and lives with you.

Let me ask you a few more questions to assess your eligibility:

**Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to ask:

**Are you responsible for Alex's care? This would mean you're looking after him and paying for things like his food, clothes, and other needs.**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely. I'm his parent and I take care of him - I pay for his food, clothes, school things, all of that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent. Just a couple more questions:

**Is Alex currently in hospital, in care, or in any residential accommodation, or does he live with you full-time at home?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Actually, Alex is in hospital at the moment. He's been there for treatment abroad.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I see. Thank you for sharing that information. This is important for determining your eligibility. Let me ask some follow-up questions about Alex's hospital stay:

**How long has Alex been in the hospital abroad?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not entirely sure of the exact timeline, to be honest.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's okay. Let me ask a related question that will help me assess your situation:

**Are you regularly spending money on Alex while he's in hospital abroad - for example, on things like clothes, toys, toiletries, or other items for him?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not really sure about that either - it's all been a bit complicated with him being away for treatment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand - this must be a difficult and complicated time for you.

Let me ask one more important question:

**Did Alex go abroad specifically to receive hospital treatment, or was he already abroad for other reasons when he became ill?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not really certain about the exact circumstances of how that all came about, to be honest.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand. Thank you for being honest about what you know and don't know about the situation.

Let me ask one final question to complete my assessment:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him.

Thank you for answering my questions. Based on the information you've provided, I'm unable to make a definitive determination about your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

**Here's why:**

Under normal circumstances, you would qualify for Child Benefit for Alex because:
- He's 8 years old (under 16)
- You're responsible for him and live in the UK
- You normally live together and you provide for his needs

**However**, Alex is currently in hospital abroad, which affects eligibility in specific ways. According to Child Benefit rules:

- Children in hospital abroad can still qualify for Child Benefit **if**:
  1. They went abroad specifically to be in hospital, **AND**
  2. You (the claimant) are back in the UK and regularly spending money on them

Unfortunately, you've indicated that you're uncertain about:
- The exact circumstances of how Alex came to be abroad for treatment
- Whether you're regularly spending money on him while he's there
- How long he's been in hospital

Without this information, I cannot determine whether you meet the exception that allows Child Benefit to continue for children in hospital abroad.

**What you should do next:**

I'd recommend contacting HMRC's Child Benefit Office directly. They can:
- Review your specific circumstances in detail
- Advise whether you qualify for Child Benefit given Alex's situation
- Let you know what information or evidence they need

You can contact them by phone or post - their contact details are available through the government's Child Benefit service.
